subject: Retention/export options for access traces — Brookside legal request
messages:
From: Jake Porter <jake.porter@brooksidehealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Legal Counsel <legal@brooksidehealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: access/audit trace export for legal hold

Hi Sofia,

We're preparing a legal preservation request and need a narrow export of admin audit and access traces for our tenant covering 2027-10-01 through 2027-12-31. Our security team asked for:
- full access log events (CSV) with timestamps, principal IDs, actions, and resource IDs;
- audit trail of admin changes (who changed which role/permission) in JSON or CSV;
- proof of residency region for the slices provided and an assurance whether any portion crossed regions during that window.

Can you confirm:
1) If Redwood can produce a single export package including both access logs and admin audit events?
2) Typical SLA for a request like this, and any charges?
3) What residency metadata you include in the export (region tags / data center ids)?

We're on a tight timeline — legal would like a proposed delivery date in the next 5 business days if feasible.

Thanks,
Jake
Jake Porter
Senior Security Ops, Brookside Health

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@brooksidehealth.com>
Cc: Legal Counsel <legal@brooksidehealth.com>
Date: 2028-01-09T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit trace export for legal hold

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers up front: yes, we can produce a combined export package with both access events and admin audit records; standard delivery for a tenant-sized export like this is 3–7 business days depending on slice size and whether we need additional legal/POC approvals. I attached a short options summary (audit_export_options.pdf) that outlines formats, typical fields, and residency metadata we include.

Important notes:
- Exports contain region tags (us-central, us-east), and we can include the physical data center codes on request as an additional column.
- For legal hold requests we recommend flagging the tenant (we'll stop automatic purges for the affected ranges) — that requires an internal approval step and a signed form if it extends past normal retention.
- If you need the export pushed to your S3, we can produce signed URLs or deliver to a pre-authorized bucket.

Proposed next step: if you confirm the exact time window and preferred delivery format (CSV vs NDJSON) I'll loop in Security (Naomi) to confirm export cadence and Compliance to estimate the final timeline/cost.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_export_options.pdf (summary),

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-01-10T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Brookside export technical constraints (refs Jake's request)

Sofia / team — quick technical notes after reviewing Jake's ask and the attachment Sofia shared. Quoting Jake below for context.

On Tue, Jan 9, 2028 at 9:15 AM Jake Porter <jake.porter@brooksidehealth.com> wrote:
> We're preparing a legal preservation request and need a narrow export of admin audit and access traces for our tenant covering 2027-10-01 through 2027-12-31.

Key points:
- Estimated payload: for an active tenant of Brookside's size, raw access events for that quarter are likely ~12–18 GB compressed; admin audit events are smaller (~200–500 MB).
- Formats: NDJSON preserves nested fields (we should use NDJSON for audit records) and CSV is fine for flattened access logs. We should offer both where feasible.
- Residency proof: we can add a per-record region_code and a delivery_manifest.csv that lists the storage nodes and snapshot hashes. We'll generate brookside_manifest.csv as part of the package.
- Export window: because this crosses our daily snapshot boundary, we'll materialize two snapshot slices (20271001-20271130, 20271201-20271231) and then merge; that adds one business day to prep.
- Legal hold: toggling the retention flag prevents background TTL deletion from running, but a signed legal hold request in writing is required to extend retention beyond contractual TTL.

Action items for ops: Sofia, can you confirm the target format and whether Brookside wants delivery to their S3 or via signed GCS URLs? Rishi — can you estimate a ballpark cost for this package and whether we should route this through Concierge for expedited handling? Marissa — can you prepare the delivery manifest template and check whether DLP scanning is required before export?

-Naomi

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jake Porter <jake.porter@brooksidehealth.com>
Cc: Legal Counsel <legal@brooksidehealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-01-11T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: access/audit trace export for legal hold

Hi Jake — quick follow-up with a concrete proposal and timeline.

Proposal summary:
1) Deliverable: combined export package containing:
   - access_events.csv (flattened CSV; columns: timestamp, principal_id, action, resource_id, region_code)
   - admin_audit.ndjson (NDJSON with change events, actor, before/after fields)
   - brookside_manifest.csv (delivery manifest with snapshot ids and region tags)
2) Delivery method: upload to Brookside S3 (please provide a pre-authorized bucket path OR we can provide signed URLs).
3) Residency metadata: each record will include region_code and snapshot_id; manifest will include physical storage node ids.
4) Timeline: prep + export = 4 business days from receipt of signed legal hold confirmation and final time window. Target delivery: 2028-01-17 if we receive confirmations by EOD 2028-01-11.
4) Cost: ballpark estimate provided after ops confirms exact payload; expect one-time export fee + data egress if applicable.

Attached is a short plan and a link to a shared folder where we'll drop the manifest and delivery checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-brookside-export-plan

If this works, please reply with: (a) confirmation of the exact date range (you listed 2027-10-01 to 2027-12-31), (b) whether you prefer S3 upload or signed URLs, and (c) a signed legal hold confirmation (we can accept an email from your Legal Counsel). Once we have those we will: create the export job, toggle the tenant hold, and schedule the snapshot materialization.

Best regards,
Sofia
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_export_options.pdf, brookside_manifest.csv

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood-inference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: 2028-01-13T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Scheduling & cost estimate for Brookside export

Sofia — confirming ops schedule and cost estimate after Naomi's tech notes:
- Storage / compute window: 6 CPU-hours + 2 GPU-minutes (for our export pipeline hashing).
- Bandwidth: estimated 18 GB outbound compressed. If they want an S3 push to an external bucket we'll add egress pricing per our standard matrix (estimate $45–90 depending on region and negotiated terms).
- Internal routing: recommend using Concierge expedite (48h SLA) since they requested <5 business days; that adds a fixed expedite fee.
- Next steps: I'll generate an invoice estimate and post it to HubSpot (HS-98324). Marissa, please finalize the manifest template and DLP checklist so we can start snapshot materialization on 2028-01-14 morning.

Rishi
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
